events.objective: Establish the symptom onset and blast radius. Determine the exact time api-gateway p99/504 rate on /v1/portfolio/* started degrading (compare to the gateway upgrade timestamp ~ earlier today 2026-03-10). Identify which downstream services serving /v1/portfolio/* are actually affected — pull per-service latency/error metrics and logs (look for timeouts, connection pool exhaustion, DB slowness, GC, CPU/memory saturation) for the portfolio path services and any shared components. Report error signatures and resource trends, and state whether the degradation is confined to the portfolio path or broader.

Build the change timeline across ALL services (not just api-gateway). List every deployment and config change around 2026-03-10 in the window preceding onset, with exact timestamps, including the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade. Map the service dependency graph for the /v1/portfolio/* path (which services the gateway calls and what they in turn depend on, including shared components like auth, caches, DBs). Search historical incidents for prior portfolio-path timeouts / gateway-upgrade fallout to find precedents.

Correlate the changes found in task b against the onset time from task a. For each deployment/config change, compare its timestamp to the precise onset of gateway p99 degradation and 504s, and check whether the affected services (from task a) match the change's target. Specifically test the HTTP/2-to-upstream hypothesis against the alternative downstream-service hypothesis: determine which explanation fits the timing and blast radius better.

events.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was flat ~200-230ms from 08:00 through 09:45, then jumped abruptly at the 09:50 bucket (avg 1849.99ms, max 4418.76ms) and stayed ~4.2-4.4s thereafter (last 4352.83).
api-gateway HTTP 5xx error rate was ~0.2% all morning until the same 09:50 bucket (avg 1.66%, max 7.18%), then held ~7.1-7.5% (last 7.25).

api-gateway WARN logs are dominated by upstream timeouts to portfolio-service on the portfolio path: 252/254 matches are 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504', first seen 09:53:53Z.

api-gateway is not resource-saturated: cpu_pct stayed ~40-46% throughout (09:00 42.29% ... 11:54 40.86%) and request_rate stayed flat ~1098-1395 req/s (09:45 1246.98 -> 09:50 1255.49), so the gateway's own load/resource did not spike at onset.
portfolio-service p99 was flat ~176-185ms until the 09:52 bucket, then jumped to avg 3744.86ms / max 4546.3ms and stayed ~4.1-4.2s; its first ERROR log is at 09:53:19Z.

portfolio-service ERROR logs (503 of 505 matched entries) show database connection-pool exhaustion on the portfolio path: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and HikariPool-1 with pool exhausted (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting up to 57).

events.answer: api-gateway p99 and 504 rate on /v1/portfolio/* degraded sharply starting ~09:50-09:53Z on 2026-03-10 (p99 204ms→~4.3s, error 0.2%→~7.2%), driven entirely by upstream timeouts to portfolio-service. portfolio-service's own p99 rose to ~4.2s at the same time, and its ERROR logs show the portfolio path failing on JDBC/Hikari connection-pool exhaustion (pool of 5, total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57). The degradation is confined to the /v1/portfolio/* path via portfolio-service; I did not verify whether the shared DB itself is also affecting other consumers.

events.statement: Only one deployment across all services in the 2026-03-09..2026-03-10T11:59Z window: api-gateway v9.3.0 (dep-5220) at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' (envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service); status 'live', rolled_back_at null.

portfolio-service config change cfg-2207: key db.pool.max_size reduced 50 -> 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z by infra-automation, description "Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource". This is ~13 minutes before the 10:05Z incident report.
Second config change: order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1 -> 0.2 at 2026-03-10T07:00:00Z by config-bot ("More request log sampling"). This is on the order path, not the portfolio path.

Dependency graph for /v1/portfolio/*: api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http); portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache); market-data-service -> redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http). Shared components on this path: ledger-db (postgres, shared=true), redis-cache (redis, shared=true). ledger-db is a shared datastore also used by order-service and payment-service; redis-cache is shared by auth-service, market-data-service and portfolio-service.

Precedent HIST-116 (2025-12-18): "HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade", services api-gateway, symptoms "504 at gateway","upstream resets","timeouts", root cause "Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default", category bad_deployment, resolution "Rolled back gateway". Lead only, not evidence about this incident.

Precedents for the DB-pool/config mechanism: HIST-115 (2025-09-25) "order-service connection pool misconfiguration" with symptoms "pool exhausted","request timed out", root cause "Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile"; and HIST-102 (2025-09-02) "Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover" on portfolio-service/ledger-db with "portfolio page timeouts","504 at gateway". Leads only.

Temporal ordering of the portfolio-path changes vs. onset: gateway HTTP/2 deploy 08:00Z, portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52Z, incident reported 10:05Z. The config change is the closest-in-time change to the report (~13 min), the gateway deploy is ~2h05m before onset.

events.answer: Across ALL services in the window 2026-03-09..2026-03-10T11:59Z there is exactly ONE deployment: api-gateway v9.3.0 (dep-5220) at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, enabling HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service — still live, not rolled back. There were TWO config changes: order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2 at 07:00Z, and — critically — portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z (cfg-2207, cost-optimisation profile 'small'), which is ~13 min before the 10:05Z report. The /v1/portfolio/* path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (shared postgres), market-data-service -> {redis-cache (shared), exchange-gateway}} and portfolio-service -> redis-cache (shared). So portfolio-service's DB pool was cut 10x and it sits on the shared ledger-db. Precedents exist for BOTH candidate mechanisms: HIST-116 (HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade, rolled back) and HIST-115 (connection pool exhausted from a wrong environment profile) + HIST-102 (portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover).

events.statement: Precise gateway onset: api-gateway p99 was ~200ms through the 09:52 bucket (200.33ms) then jumped to 4418.76ms in the 09:53 bucket — a clean one-bucket step, no ramp. The 09:52 bucket (09:52:00-09:53:00) was still normal.

portfolio-service p99 shows the identical one-bucket step at the same instant: 172.69ms in the 09:52 bucket → 4250.91ms in the 09:53 bucket. Gateway and the downstream service degraded in the same minute, not sequentially.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use exactly tracks the cfg-2207 config change: it held ~11.3-12.7 connections through the 09:52 bucket (11.89), then was pinned at exactly 5.0 (max 5) from the 09:53 bucket onward — i.e. the pool ceiling dropped from ~50 to the configured max_size 5, coinciding within one minute with cfg-2207 at 09:52Z.

Blast radius is confined to the portfolio path despite HTTP/2 being enabled to BOTH portfolio-service and order-service: order-service p99 stayed flat at ~145-154ms across the entire 08:00-11:52Z window (e.g. 09:52 avg 150.3ms, 10:00 avg 151.02ms, last 11:52 avg 148.22ms), and api-gateway logged zero order-service/timeout WARN matching 'order'.

The first gateway 504 log on the portfolio path is at 09:53:53Z ('upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504'), ~1m53s after the 09:52Z config change and ~1h54m after the 08:00Z gateway HTTP/2 deploy — consistent with errors beginning in the 09:53 bucket.

Timing/blast-radius fit favours the pool config over the HTTP/2 deploy: the HTTP/2 upgrade was at 08:00Z but the gateway stayed healthy (~200ms p99) for ~1h52m after it, and both HTTP/2 targets did not degrade together (order-service flat). The 09:52Z db.pool.max_size 50->5 change is ~1-2 min before the single sharp onset, and the pool metric pins at exactly 5.0 in the same bucket. ledger-db itself shows no WARN/ERROR logs in 09:00-11:59Z, so the DB is not the failing component.

events.description: Query for api-gateway WARN logs containing 'order' returned 0 matches, so I can confirm no order-path gateway timeouts but cannot rule out order-path errors emitted above WARN or logged elsewhere.

ledger-db query_logs returned 0 matches — the log query itself worked but ledger-db appears to emit no WARN+ logs (or no logs) in the window, so it is not confirmable that ledger-db was healthy from logs.

events.answer: The HTTP/2-to-upstream hypothesis does NOT fit the timing or blast radius; the portfolio-service DB-pool config change does. The HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220, 08:00Z) targeted both portfolio-service and order-service, yet the gateway stayed healthy (~200ms p99) for ~1h52m afterward and order-service never degraded (p99 flat ~150ms, zero order-path gateway timeouts). Instead, api-gateway and portfolio-service p99 both stepped up in the SAME bucket (09:53Z, from ~200ms/~173ms to ~4.4s/~4.25s), exactly when portfolio-service's db_pool_in_use dropped from ~12 to exactly 5.0 — pinning it to the cfg-2207 db.pool.max_size 50->5 change at 09:52Z. The blast radius (portfolio path only, pool exhaustion, DB itself healthy) matches the config change, not the gateway deploy.

api-gateway HTTP/2-to-upstream envoy upgrade (dep-5220) broke connections to portfolio-service
ledger-db / shared datastore degradation stalled portfolio-service's JDBC pool
Traffic/load spike unrelated to any deploy saturated the portfolio path

Determine the exact time api-gateway p99/504 rate on /v1/portfolio/* started degrading (compare to the gateway upgrade timestamp ~ earlier today 2026-03-10). Identify which downstream services serving /v1/portfolio/* are actually affected — pull per-service latency/error metrics and logs (look for timeouts, connection pool exhaustion, DB slowness, GC, CPU/memory saturation) for the portfolio path services and any shared components. Report error signatures and resource trends, and state whether the degradation is confined to the portfolio path or broader.
tasks.answer: api-gateway p99 and 504 rate on /v1/portfolio/* degraded sharply starting ~09:50-09:53Z on 2026-03-10 (p99 204ms→~4.3s, error 0.2%→~7.2%), driven entirely by upstream timeouts to portfolio-service. portfolio-service's own p99 rose to ~4.2s at the same time, and its ERROR logs show the portfolio path failing on JDBC/Hikari connection-pool exhaustion (pool of 5, total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57). The degradation is confined to the /v1/portfolio/* path via portfolio-service; I did not verify whether the shared DB itself is also affecting other consumers.

tasks.objective: Build the change timeline across ALL services (not just api-gateway). List every deployment and config change around 2026-03-10 in the window preceding onset, with exact timestamps, including the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade. Map the service dependency graph for the /v1/portfolio/* path (which services the gateway calls and what they in turn depend on, including shared components like auth, caches, DBs). Search historical incidents for prior portfolio-path timeouts / gateway-upgrade fallout to find precedents.
tasks.answer: Across ALL services in the window 2026-03-09..2026-03-10T11:59Z there is exactly ONE deployment: api-gateway v9.3.0 (dep-5220) at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, enabling HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service — still live, not rolled back. There were TWO config changes: order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2 at 07:00Z, and — critically — portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z (cfg-2207, cost-optimisation profile 'small'), which is ~13 min before the 10:05Z report. The /v1/portfolio/* path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (shared postgres), market-data-service -> {redis-cache (shared), exchange-gateway}} and portfolio-service -> redis-cache (shared). So portfolio-service's DB pool was cut 10x and it sits on the shared ledger-db. Precedents exist for BOTH candidate mechanisms: HIST-116 (HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade, rolled back) and HIST-115 (connection pool exhausted from a wrong environment profile) + HIST-102 (portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover).

tasks.objective: Correlate the changes found in task b against the onset time from task a. tasks.answer: The HTTP/2-to-upstream hypothesis does NOT fit the timing or blast radius; the portfolio-service DB-pool config change does. The HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220, 08:00Z) targeted both portfolio-service and order-service, yet the gateway stayed healthy (~200ms p99) for ~1h52m afterward and order-service never degraded (p99 flat ~150ms, zero order-path gateway timeouts). Instead, api-gateway and portfolio-service p99 both stepped up in the SAME bucket (09:53Z, from ~200ms/~173ms to ~4.4s/~4.25s), exactly when portfolio-service's db_pool_in_use dropped from ~12 to exactly 5.0 — pinning it to the cfg-2207 db.pool.max_size 50->5 change at 09:52Z. The blast radius (portfolio path only, pool exhaustion, DB itself healthy) matches the config change, not the gateway deploy.
